Lessons.Title: Linear Functions
ExplanationParagraphs: Original learning aims: identify and interpret linear models f(x)=mx+b, determine whether behavior increases/decreases/is constant, calculate rate from points, write slope-intercept and point-slope equations, and model tables/contexts.
Slope is a constant rate (change in output)/(change in input). The sign determines increasing or decreasing behavior. A line has slope m and initial value b=f(0).
Given a point and slope, use y−y1=m(x−x1). Given two points, first compute m, then solve for b.
An actual model should state units, physical domain and the meaning of its initial value. Tables require a constant rate on every pair of neighboring measurements.
Independent Edulytics cool-down: (a) Find f(x)=mx+b through (−1,2) and (3,10). (b) What do slope and intercept mean in C(n)=150+8n? (c) Decide if x=5 represents y as a function of x.
Independent Try It 1 — Identify slope and initial value. For f(t)=8t+15, state initial value, rate, and behavior.
Independent Try It 2 — Classify by slope. Classify f(x)=−3x+7, g(x)=0x+5 and h(x)=2x−1.
Independent Try It 3 — Two-point slope. Compute slope through (−2,4),(2,10).
Independent Try It 4 — Point-slope equation. Find line slope 4 through (2,−3).
Independent Try It 5 — Cost from fixed charge. With initial charge $40 and $12 per item, write C(n) and compute C(5).
Independent Try It 6 — Table linearity. A table x=0,2,4,6 has outputs 3,7,11,15. Find f.

KeyConcepts.Title: Linear equation
KeyConcepts.Definition: A linear function has form f(x)=mx+b with a constant rate.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Slope m describes output change per input; b=f(0).

KeyConcepts.Title: Slope from coordinates
KeyConcepts.Rule: Both coordinate differences must follow matching endpoint order.

KeyConcepts.Title: Increasing/decreasing
KeyConcepts.Rule: Positive slopes increase, negatives decrease; zero slope is constant.

KeyConcepts.Title: Point-slope form
KeyConcepts.Definition: A line through (x1,y1) with slope m satisfies y−y1=m(x−x1).

KeyConcepts.Title: Linear model units
KeyConcepts.Definition: Each unit increase in x changes output by m output units.
KeyConcepts.Rule: State physical domain, units and initial value.

KeyConcepts.Title: Linear table test
KeyConcepts.Definition: Successive data pairs lie on one line iff all pairwise slopes match.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Use Δy/Δx even for unequal input gaps.

KeyConcepts.Title: Vertical and horizontal lines
KeyConcepts.Definition: A vertical line x=c is not a function y=f(x) on a multi-y graph.
KeyConcepts.Rule: A horizontal line y=c is a constant function.

SummaryPoints: Slope is a constant output change per unit input.
Two distinct points determine one line.
Modeling requires appropriate units and admissible domains.

Visuals.Title: First-party uniform linear growth
Visuals.Description: Equal input increments yield equal output changes.

Visuals.Title: Linear and nonlinear table distinction
Visuals.Description: The middle row demonstrates constant difference; bottom row does not.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Assuming a nonlinear table is linear.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Slopes differ across equal input changes.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Calling x=5 a linear function y=f(x).
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: A vertical line has many outputs for the same input.
